title: Bahrain Petroleum Company → New York, cable messages in a pad cipher, with censor's plain-language copies
correspondents: Ward Anderson / W. P. Anderson, BAPCO Bahrain ↔ Bahrain Petroleum Company, New York
shelfmark: British Library, IOR/R/15/2/450 (File 10/23 Code Messages - BAPCO); system described in IOR/R/15/2/423 (File 10/5 BAPCO Codes)
folio_note: 196 images; typed 5-letter groups (e.g. f. 4r COSLE QQQQQ BABIX ...) interleaved with 'Outward cable ... Service: CODE' plain copies for the censor
status: Not on DECODE. 423 (OCR'd on QDL): code approved Jan 1944 'on the understanding that the pad is not worked through more than once'; security officer judged it of small resistance to cryptography; plain-language copies to the censor were a condition. Pairs not yet matched
why: A documented WWII commercial pad cipher with plaintext-ciphertext pairs; shows how a company code was vetted and used under censorship

title: Political Resident Bushire, Muscat and others → Political Agent Bahrain, telegrams in Government Telegraph Code / Indian Word Code

shelfmark: British Library, IOR/R/15/2/955 ('206 Cypher Codes. Correspondence re.')
folio_note: 40 images; handwritten Indo-European Telegraph Department forms, ten-letter code words (f. 3r: 13 words, no gloss); some telegrams glossed in pencil
status: Not on DECODE. Catalogue: 'copies of telegrams written in cypher, some of which have the decoded words written above in pencil'. IOR/R/15/2/1466-1467 hold Indian Word Code 1924 supplements (addressee code words only, as sampled)
why: Unglossed Government of India codebook telegrams from the Gulf, 1918-26; a test of reconstructing a one-part official codebook from glossed siblings
